verdicts.why: Key A is the correct definition of globalisation and the other options are clearly wrong. The option lengths were uneven (A about 105 characters against C about 82), which cues the key, so distractors B and D were lengthened to balance the set. Key unchanged.

The WTO came into existence on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement and succeeded GATT. Distractors 1944 (Bretton Woods), 1948 (GATT) and 2001 (China's accession) are each a real event; key D is unique.
Liberalisation = (II), privatisation = (I), FDI = (III), outsourcing = (IV). Key B is the only option matching all four pairs; the other three options each contain at least two wrong pairs.
Chronology is Bretton Woods 1944, India NEP 1991, WTO 1995, Seattle protests 1999, giving (C),(D),(A),(B). Key C is unique and the distractor orderings are each wrong at a distinct point.
Statements B (MNCs operate across borders) and D (IMF and World Bank set up at Bretton Woods 1944) are correct; A and C are false. Key D is the only pair of correct statements.

Key A (balance of payments crisis) is correct. Distractor B (WTO expelling India in 1991) was absurd because the WTO did not exist until 1995, so it was replaced with a plausible but false RBI decision on foreign banks. Distractor C was reworded to a false 1991 nationalisation by the Government of India (the real nationalisations were 1969 and 1980) and the explanation was updated to match. Key unchanged.

Economic, cultural and technological dimensions (A, C, D) are standard dimensions of globalisation. Option B, which describes political decision-making confined to one nation-state, is the negation of the political dimension, so key B is unique for a NOT question.

Both statements are true and the relaxation of capital controls is the cause of greater financial integration, so R explains A. Key C is correct; the standard A/R distractors are each wrong on a different point.

Key A (IMF for short-term foreign exchange shortage, then World Bank for long-term dam finance) is correct and the WTO distractors are clearly wrong. The difficulty label was 'hard' for a single-step institution-matching item, so it was changed to 'medium'. Key unchanged.
